rows.what the ink shows: Several thick, nearly coincident horizontal cancellation strokes cover the bodies and joins of this phrase. A few upright tips and a dot survive above them, and one hooked descender survives below near the middle, compatible with the g of voisinage; the surrounding letters and the short outer words cannot be separated securely even at 4×.

At the end of the rotated proposition, after il suffit, the writing reduces to overlapping hooked/looped strokes and a short rightward mark; tall strokes from the intersecting main writing also enter the margin. The enlarged line does not provide distinct letter groups sufficient to verify all three proposed words or to replace them with a different phrase.

The deleted capital has an upright stem and a strong diagonal lower-right leg. Two crossing cancellation strokes obscure the upper-right region where an R bowl would have to close, so the exposed strokes could also belong to K. A paired lobed mark is visible raised to its right, supporting the infinity superscript but not resolving the capital.

Above a struck-through remnant after prop. 3, the surviving reading begins with a small open cup rising into a narrow loop, followed by a tall rounded d-like stroke. The following low linked strokes and separate shallow terminal curl support the ci-dessus sequence; it is the writing above the cancellation that is read here.

Immediately before the two parallel bars, the word has only a shallow initial bowl/crest followed by a long almost level exit. There is no securely separate second hump or internal loop that distinguishes n from a rapidly contracted m, and the terminal e is flattened into the exit. The source ne remains uncertain.

The first group begins with an upright t-like stroke, has a long low join that bends below the baseline into the j region, and ends in a small rightward s-like hook. A separate tall curved l and its low return follow, then a tall f with a descending hook and extended low continuation. These three separated groups support toujours la forme.

At the next line start, a long descending initial p returns sharply upward; two small dots sit over the compressed interior strokes. The latter portion has a narrow loop/rounded join, then a tall final l with a low rightward curl, supporting principale.
